source_text: Nam scribens ad eum, quem miratur studiosum esse librorum suorum, cum sit militiae sudoribus occupatus, indicat ab Alypio chartulas ad se fuisse delatas, quae ita superscriptae essent: Capitula de libro Augustini quem scripsit, contra quae de libris pauca decerpsi. Hic video eum, qui tuae Praestantiae ista scripta direxit, de nescio quibus libris ea, causa, quantum existimo, celerioris responsionis, ne tuam differret instantiam, voluisse decerpere. Qui autem sint isti libri cum cogitarem, eos esse arbitratus sum, quorum mentionem Iulianus facit in epistola quam Romam misit, cuius exemplum simul ad me usque pervenit. Ibi quippe ait: Dicunt etiam istas, quae modo aguntur, nuptias a Deo institutas non fuisse, quod in libro Augustini legitur, contra quem ego modo quattuor libellis respondi. Et post haec verba infert iterum suis sermonibus: Credo ex his libellis ista decerpta sunt; unde melius fortasse fuerat, ut universo ipsi operi eius, quod quattuor voluminibus explicavit, refellendo et redarguendo nostra elaboraret intentio; nisi et ego responsionem differre noluissem; sicut nec tu transmissionem scriptorum, quibus respondendum est, distulisti [n13] . Ostendit ergo hic apertissime excerpta illa suspicari se de opere meo tumultuarie fuisse collecta; integros autem ignorare libros, quibus tamen audet se dicere respondere potuisse.
pass_a_gloss: For writing to him whom he wonders is studious of his books, although occupied with the sweats of military service, he indicates that little papers were brought to him by Alypius, which were headed thus: 'Heads from a book of Augustine which he wrote, against which I have plucked a few things from books.' 'Here I see that he who directed these writings to Your Eminence wanted to pluck them from I-know-not-what books, for the cause, as I estimate, of a quicker answer, lest he put off your urgency. But when I was thinking which those books are, I judged them to be those of which Julian makes mention in the letter which he sent to Rome, a copy of which reached even to me at the same time. For there he says: They even say that these marriages which are now being carried on were not instituted by God, which is read in Augustine's book, against which I have now answered in four little books.' And after these words he brings in again with his own speeches: 'I believe these things were plucked from those little books; whence it would perhaps have been better that our attention should work at refuting and convicting that whole work of his which he unfolded in four volumes; except that I too was unwilling to put off the answer; just as you did not delay the sending of the writings to which answer must be made.' He shows therefore here most openly that he suspects those excerpts were collected from my work in a scramble; but that he does not know the intact books, to which nevertheless he dares to say he could have answered.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: Writing to the man whose devotion to his books astonishes him, occupied as that man is with the hardships of military service, he reports that Alypius brought him some sheets headed: 'Passages from a book Augustine wrote, against which I have excerpted a few things from some books.' Augustine continues: 'Here I see that the person who sent these writings to Your Eminence wanted to excerpt them from books unknown to me, in order, as I suppose, to obtain a quicker reply and not postpone your urgent request. When I considered what books these might be, I supposed they were those Julian mentions in the letter he sent to Rome, a copy of which reached me at the same time. There he says: “They even say that the marriages now taking place were not instituted by God. This can be read in Augustine's book, which I have just answered in four little books.”' After these words Augustine adds in his own voice: 'I believe these passages were excerpted from those little books. It might therefore have been better for me to devote my attention to refuting and disproving the whole work he set out in four volumes, except that I too was unwilling to delay my reply, just as you did not delay sending the writings that required an answer' (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.2). Here, then, he shows perfectly clearly that he suspects those excerpts were hastily collected from my work. He does not know the complete books, yet dares to say that he could have answered them.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
